layouts.Q: [1,16,16,128] as the graph already has it
layouts.K: transposed first: attention_dot computes A[M,K] @ B[K,N], so K has to arrive as [1,16,128,512]
layouts.output: [1,16,16,128], which is what the fused op returned

bugs_found_and_fixed.symptom: NaN everywhere on the first attempt
bugs_found_and_fixed.cause: the mask kernel does `tl.load(Position + query)`, so Position is one causal boundary PER QUERY ROW, not a scalar. A [1] buffer meant query >= 1 read past it, a negative garbage boundary masked the whole row, and a fully masked row makes softmax NaN.
bugs_found_and_fixed.fix: position workspace is [sequence], filled with start + arange(S)

bugs_found_and_fixed.cause: attention_dot is `A[M,K] @ B[K,N]` -- B is NOT transposed. So QK needs K as [heads, head_dim, total], but the graph carries [heads, total, head_dim]. I had assumed Q@K^T.
bugs_found_and_fixed.fix: transpose K with a layout kernel first. The library only had layout_k for 16- and 17-slot contexts, so layout_k_16x512x128 was added to tools/generate_elementwise.py and built through the full Triton -> triton-riscv -> MLIR -> Buddy lowering -> NR chain
bugs_found_and_fixed.how_it_was_found: a standalone host test of attention_qk with known inputs against numpy, which showed the output matched neither Q@K^T nor any scaled variant; reading kernels.py's attention_dot then gave the layout outright

remaining_replacements.rope: cos/sin are computed in the graph; they would have to become explicit call arguments
remaining_replacements.kv_cache_write: it updates a graph input in place, so it needs an out-parameter form rather than a returned value

board.note: host-only work; the full-model run was not disturbed

compiled_code_comparison.reading: RVV rises 156 -> 245, so more of the work is vectorised, but the total instruction count RISES rather than falls. That is a warning, not a result: instruction count is not a runtime proxy when the code being removed is a LOOP. A nested linalg attention can be a few hundred instructions executed many thousands of times, while the five kernels that replace it contribute their own few thousand instructions once.
compiled_code_comparison.correction: the first version of this comparison accidentally read the 28-layer image (286,910 instructions) as the baseline; both entries are now one-layer builds
compiled_code_comparison.conclusion: the speed effect of the attention replacement cannot be established from the audit; it needs a board measurement

ready_to_measure.plan: the 1-layer interactive-free image; the run takes a few minutes, so it can replace the per-layer projection (validation/memory-plan-w8a8.json) with a measured number as soon as the board frees
ready_to_measure.what_to_compare: launch cycles for prefill against the 5,515,994,658 measured for the same layer without the attention replacement
